1.reason: read_plan's deps surface lives in reckon/mcp.py, held by one-call-explains-any-ref until it lands; it is carried as a new section of a-project-reads-as-one-picture

findings.text: assert _row(report, "x")["slug"] == "x" cannot fail: _row only returns a row whose slug already matches, and line 148 repeats the assertion at line 130, so the case named 'a section wait never holds its whole plan' asserts nothing about plan-level holding and would not redden if the followup wait were classified as a plan blocker.

_resolve_plan_ref resolves a newly admitted 'y@f-1' ref through dependency_row_state(data, parsed.stage) with stage None, so the read_plan deps surface reports the whole plan's status and silently drops the followup the extended grammar now allows.

excluding followup edges from declared_section_refs leaves the section half of a combined 'y#s2@f-1' ref unregistered, so a blocked run whose text names y#s2 raises an undeclared-wait false positive for a wait the section did declare.
the malformed-ref refusal here, and the same wording at line 1014, still tells the author the grammar is [project:]slug[#section] in the commit that extends it with an @followup suffix.
